DOUBLE_DECODE_BYPASS.description: Compares live server behavior on a singly-encoded vs. double-encoded path-traversal-style payload. A discrepancy (double-encoded request gets further than the single-encoded one) is evidence the input is decoded/canonicalized more than once before validation.

CRLF_HEADER_REFLECTION.description: Injects an encoded CRLF sequence plus a marker header name/value into common redirect/reflection query parameters and checks whether the marker comes back as a literal response header. This is a reflection-based approximation of V4.2.4 (app-level header injection), not a protocol-level HTTP/2/3 frame-validation test.

OPEN_REDIRECT_LIVE.description: Confirms, against the live target, whether common redirect/callback query parameters — or a forged Host header — drive an unvalidated external redirect. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static UNVALIDATED_REDIRECT taint rule flags at the source level.

REQUEST_SMUGGLING.description: Sends a request with an ambiguous Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding combination immediately followed by a distinctly-marked second request on the same connection, then checks whether the marker leaks into the first response — evidence the front-end/back-end chain disagrees on request framing. Best-effort indicator, not a full exploit chain. Gated behind active_mode: a real desync can affect other users' traffic on shared infrastructure, unlike this engine's other checks.

CSRF_TOKEN_NOT_VALIDATED.description: Fetches the target, finds the first state-changing (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) form containing a CSRF-token-shaped hidden field, then resubmits the form with that field dropped. A non-4xx response means the server accepted a state-changing request without validating the anti-CSRF token. Gated behind active_mode: a genuinely unprotected form really does perform the action, unlike this engine's read-only checks.

UNAUTHENTICATED_ACCESS_ALLOWED.description: Requests the target once through the scan's authenticated session, then again with no credentials at all. If the anonymous request also returns 2xx where the authenticated one did, the endpoint doesn't appear to actually require authentication — forced-browsing / missing function-level access control. Only runs when the scan has an authenticated session configured; otherwise there's nothing to compare against.

REFLECTED_XSS_LIVE.description: Replays each query parameter the URL already carries (e.g. crawler-discovered /search?q=...) with a unique inert marker tag, then checks whether it comes back unescaped. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static XSS taint rule flags at the source level. Only tests params the URL already has — unlike OPEN_REDIRECT_LIVE/CRLF_HEADER_REFLECTION, reflected XSS has no small fixed universe of semantically-meaningful param names to guess blindly.

SQL_INJECTION_LIVE.description: For each query parameter the URL already carries, appends an always-true (' OR '1'='1) and an always-false (' OR '1'='2) SQL boolean to the existing value and compares the two responses — a real unparameterized query returns visibly different results for the two, or leaks a DB driver error message outright. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static SQL_INJECTION taint rule flags at the source level. Gated behind active_mode: on a write-context param these payloads reach a real query, same risk class as CSRF_TOKEN_NOT_VALIDATED.
